hardware.tested_state: existing flashed firmware with companion request-bound serial smoke

procedure: Added the optional NostrSeal/lab hardware_companion_serial_smoke.py script for attached-board checks outside CI.
Exported ESP-IDF v5.5.4 from /Users/vincenzo/esp/esp-idf-v5.5.4/export.sh in the same shell invocation used for hardware smoke.
Verified idf.py, esptool.py, and /dev/cu.usbmodem1101 before opening the board port.
Used NostrSeal/companion nseal request to generate get_capabilities, get_signing_status, get_public_key, and sign_event requests with explicit lab request ids.
Used NostrSeal/companion nseal serial-frame wrap-request to encode each request frame.
Sent each frame to the attached ESP32 over USB serial and captured the first nseal1f protocol response while ignoring device log lines.
Used NostrSeal/companion nseal serial-frame unwrap-response --request to validate each captured response against its original request before accepting output.
expected_result: The attached board answers companion-generated get_capabilities, get_signing_status, and get_public_key serial requests with ok responses, and rejects a companion-generated sign_event request with signing_disabled until production gates pass.
observed_result: The optional lab hardware companion serial smoke passed for get_capabilities with request_id lab-companion-hw-capabilities, get_signing_status with request_id lab-companion-hw-signing-status, and get_public_key with request_id lab-companion-hw-public-key. Each response unwrapped through the companion request-bound serial path with ok: true. The sign-event-disabled mode generated a sign_event request from the shared basic kind 1 fixture with request_id lab-companion-hw-sign-event-disabled; the attached board returned error.code signing_disabled, and companion request-bound unwrap accepted only that matched disabled response.
limitations: This is protocol smoke using the existing flashed firmware image; it is not a new build or flash report.
This is not a new manual visual display inspection.
This smoke exercises sign_event only as a disabled-signing refusal path; it does not produce or verify a real signature.

The run does not validate production trusted-display acceptance, production physical-control acceptance, key provisioning, storage, secure boot, flash encryption, debug lock, companion signed-output verification for real signatures, or real signing.
sign_event is expected to remain signing_disabled until every production signing gate is satisfied.
